monthly_review.summary: This month shows a clear strategic shift toward lower-intensity, higher-volume aerobic development — evidenced by increased Z1/Z2 time and reduced HR, though at the cost of pace and aerobic TE compared to last month.
monthly_review.highlight: Zone distribution shifted dramatically: Z1+Z2 rose from 55% to 86% this month, while Z3–Z5 dropped from 45% to 13%, indicating a deliberate — but incomplete — transition into foundational aerobic base building.

goal_tracker.message: You need 11.8 more km across 4 additional sessions (avg 2.95 km/session) in the remaining 19 days to match last month’s volume — achievable with two 4km runs and two 2km easy runs.

insights.title: Efficiency dip aligns with slower pacing and longer ground contact
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency fell from 13.66 to 13.09 m/sec per bpm; notably, ground contact time increased from avg ~305ms (last month estimated) to 318ms this month (e.g., 351ms on 9.5km run), suggesting reduced neuromuscular elasticity at slower paces.

insights.title: Near-total absence of threshold and VO2 max stimulus
insights.body: Z4 and Z5 accounted for 0% this month vs 19% last month (15% Z4 + 4% Z5), meaning no structured efforts above ~85% HRmax — critical for maintaining aerobic power and VO2 max trajectory.

insights.title: Cadence improved despite slower pace and shorter stride
insights.body: Avg cadence rose from 142 to 143 spm, and recent runs show cadence increasing from 133 (May 2) to 150 (May 13) — even as pace slowed and stride length remained low (66–71cm), indicating better turnover control and potential form adaptation to fatigue resistance.

insights.title: Long run dominates volume but lacks progressive overload
insights.body: The 9.5km run (May 6) is 36% of this month’s total distance and occurred at 131 bpm (Z1), yet it produced only 3.0 TE — below last month’s avg aerobic TE of 3.1 — suggesting diminishing returns without slight intensity variation or terrain change.

recommendations.action: Add 3 × 90-second strides at 4:15–4:25 min/km (530–500 sec/km) after your next 5km easy run, with full 2-min walk recovery between.
recommendations.reason: Your best recent pace is 530 sec/km (May 13), and last month you hit 428 sec/km — reintroducing brief neuromuscular priming will support cadence gains and prevent efficiency decay.

recommendations.action: Do one 45-minute Zone 2 run (HR 128–138 bpm) with cadence consciously held ≥145 spm using metronome or audio cue.
recommendations.reason: Your May 13 run hit 150 spm at 553 sec/km — proving capability; anchoring that cadence in Zone 2 builds endurance-specific neuromuscular efficiency.

recommendations.action: Replace one upcoming easy run with a 3km progression run: first km @ 9:30 min/km (570 sec/km), second @ 9:00 (540), third @ 8:30 (510).
recommendations.reason: This introduces mild Z3 stimulus (HR likely 140–145 bpm based on May 2 & 12 data) to counteract the complete absence of Z3–Z5 this month while staying within safe aerobic load.

weekly_focus.description: Strengthen neuromuscular coordination at sustainable intensities to improve efficiency, support longer ground contact tolerance, and rebuild aerobic power without overstressing recovery.
